name: comp-51
title: Password Strength Input
description: A password input with an eye toggle, a thin progress bar that grows and warms from red to green, and a checklist of four rules whose crosses turn into green ticks as you type.
use: A sign-up or reset form where people need to see, while typing, which password rules they still owe.
avoid: Rules, wording and thresholds are hardcoded, so a different password policy needs a source edit.
a11y: Bar is a labelled progressbar and met state is hidden text, but the width animation never checks reduced-motion. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded text field sits under a small heading label, with a faded eye icon at its right end. Below it a slim rounded track runs across the width, then a bold status line and four rows of small text, each prefixed by a grey cross or a green tick.
behaves: Typing fills the bar from the left and the status line changes from an empty prompt to weak, then strong; the bar animates its width and colour over half a second as each rule passes. Pressing the eye swaps the dots for plain characters and flips the icon and its label.
customise: It takes no props: the label, the four regex rules and the colour thresholds sit in the file, so changing policy wording or colours means editing the source.
weight: light: One text field, a four-item list and a CSS width transition with no loop.
demo: Label "Input with password strength indicator", placeholder "Password" and four rule lines such as "At least 1 number".
polishWhy: Tidy spacing and a clear colour story; the rule list itself is a plain default stack.
